headline: Six days now without a run — the restart pair never took root. The Åre block still holds the base, but strength and a fresh threshold read remain untouched gaps.
confidence_reasons: No recent activity data in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is defined more by what's absent than what's present. The recent 4-week block sits dramatically higher than the prior one, but nearly all of that came from the Åre trail volume and the two short faster runs — and none of it has landed in the last six days. Running has gone quiet at exactly the point the restart needed a third session to become rhythm. Strength stays the most degraded corner: no session in almost two weeks, and the year-to-date rate is drifting below where it once sat. Steps remain genuinely high even on rest days, so the background athletic load is holding the athlete's floor up while structured training pauses — that daily movement is doing real work here. Nothing in the load data suggests a problem worth caution; this reads as a lull in structured input against a well-stocked base, not fatigue or strain.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is unmistakably front-loaded by the Åre block — a large durability spike sitting inside an otherwise moderate cadence. Year-to-date, the distance gap over last year is enormous, which tells you the base has genuinely deepened, not just spiked once. But the shape of the last fortnight is a flattening, not a build: a big trail block, two sharp efforts, then silence. That's consistent with a transition between focuses rather than a coherent progression — which is fine for a year-round hybrid athlete, but it's now lasted long enough that the next block needs to declare a direction rather than stay in limbo.
sections.threshold: The threshold reading is now two months old and remains the stalest signal on the board. The two short faster runs late in August both reached genuine top-end range, which is at least indirect evidence the aerobic ceiling hasn't gone anywhere — but they were mixed-intent efforts, not a clean tempo, so they can't refresh the number. Until a committed threshold-style effort lands, treat the current figure as a floor from a fitter, denser period rather than a current measurement.
sections.zones: The distribution splits cleanly into two populations. The Åre runs sat almost entirely in Z1 — pure time-on-feet, exactly what long trail durability should look like, and correctly kept slow. The two August restart runs, by contrast, carried real Z3 with brief Z4 touches — genuinely mixed sessions, not steady aerobic work, and the max HR on both confirms real intensity rather than an average hiding a range. That's an appropriate contrast for a hybrid block: durability slow, sharpening sharp. What's missing is the connective middle — a sustained tempo that neither the trail nor the short-sharp runs provide.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing in the strength HR history is out of pattern — the sessions cluster in low aerobic range as expected for functional work, and the most recent logged session simply carries no HR at all. Across the runs, avg-to-max spreads behave sensibly for the effort type. There's no source-agreement issue worth flagging here.
sections.calendar: The running streak is intact by week, but the texture underneath it has thinned to almost nothing — the last real cluster of activity was the Åre trip, and since then it's been sparse and increasingly cold. Strength consistency, by contrast, has effectively lapsed: no anchor in nearly two weeks and a streak sitting at zero. The calendar is telling you the athlete is holding the minimum viable rhythm on running while strength has quietly dropped out of the picture entirely.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance PBs were set almost exactly a year ago in a sharpening-heavy period. The two recent fast runs show the top-end range is still accessible, so a 5K or 10K PB isn't unrealistic on paper — but it would require a focused speed block that the current transition-limbo pattern isn't yet delivering. Nothing about the present base points toward an imminent attempt; the raw ingredients are there, the structure isn't.

watch_items: Watch whether any run lands at all this week — the gap has now stretched long enough that the priority is simply re-establishing contact, not cadence quality.
Watch whether strength reappears in any form — it's been the quiet corner for weeks and now has no recent anchor whatsoever.
Watch whether the next block finally picks a lane — trail durability or speed — rather than continuing to alternate without committing.
Watch for a clean sustained tempo effort, which is the one session type that would both refresh the stale threshold and fill the missing middle of the zone distribution.
